- paseo-advisor: Spin up a single agent as an advisor — second opinion on the current task. Use when the user says "advisor", "second opinion", "what does X think", or wants an outside take without delegating the work itself.
- paseo-committee: Form a committee of two high-reasoning agents to step back, do root cause analysis, and produce a plan. Use when stuck, looping, tunnel-visioning, or facing a hard planning problem.
- paseo-handoff: Hand off the current task to another agent with full context. Use when the user says "handoff", "hand off", "hand this to", or wants to pass work to another agent.
- paseo-loop: Run an agent loop until an exit condition is met. Use when the user says "loop", "babysit", "keep trying until", "check every X", "watch", or wants iterative autonomous execution.
- skills: Reference codebase for Crates. Use this skill when you need to understand the structure, implementation patterns, or code details of the Crates project.
- zeroclaw: Configure and operate ZeroClaw autonomous AI infrastructure. Use when user mentions zeroclaw CLI, needs to setup/configure zeroclaw, asks about 'zeroclaw providers', 'zeroclaw channels', 'autonomous AI agent', or wants to run LLMs on low-cost hardware (Raspberry Pi, ESP32, Arduino).
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. # OPBlob SHM Handoff

## What Changed

- Added real runtime materialization commands to `crates/op-blob/src/bin/opblob.rs`:
  - `opblob seal-shm`
  - `opblob seal-plugins <dir>`
- The commands discover canonical plugin schemas through `op_plugins::DefaultPluginRegistry::load_all_plugins()` using `op_state_store::MemoryStore`.
- The commands seal real `PluginSchema` objects into the SHM blob catalog at `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs`.
- Added `op-plugins` and `tokio` dependencies to `crates/op-blob/Cargo.toml`.
- Fixed `crates/op-blob/src/blob.rs` so method manifest generation does not assume the `HashMap` key equals `MethodDecl.name`.
- Built and installed `/usr/local/bin/opblob`.
- Patched `/etc/s6/sv/op-dbus/run` to run `/usr/local/bin/opblob seal-shm` before starting `op-dbus`.
- Also added `OP_DBUS_GRPC_LISTEN="${OP_DBUS_GRPC_LISTEN:-10.200.0.1:50051}"` to `/etc/s6/sv/op-dbus/run`.

## Verified

- `cargo check -p op-blob` passes.
- `cargo build --release -p op-blob --bin opblob` passes.
- `/usr/local/bin/opblob seal-shm` succeeds.
- `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs` contains 62 `.blob` files.
- `/usr/local/bin/opblob catalog /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs` parses the active catalog.
- `/usr/local/bin/opblob inspect /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/zeroclaw.*.blob` parses and shows canonical D-Bus path `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/zeroclaw`.
- `xray` blob exists.
- Installed binary hash matched release build:
  - `target/release/opblob`
  - `/usr/local/bin/opblob`

## Important Runtime State

- `/etc/s6/sv/op-dbus/run` has the blob hook and the bind fix.
- The blob hook was copied into `/run/service/op-dbus/run`.
- The bind fix was not copied into `/run/service/op-dbus/run` before interruption.
- `op-dbus` was failing because it tried to bind `10.200.0.2:50051`.
- Current host has `ovsbr0` as `10.200.0.1/30`; no `10.200.0.2` address exists.
- Manual run with blob hook disabled showed `Cannot assign requested address (os error 99)`.
- This failure is unrelated to `opblob`; `/usr/local/bin/opblob seal-shm` exits cleanly.

## Next Commands

```sh
sudo -n install -m 0755 /etc/s6/sv/op-dbus/run /run/service/op-dbus/run
sh -n /run/service/op-dbus/run
sudo -n s6-svc -r /run/service/op-dbus
sleep 2
sudo -n s6-svstat /run/service/op-dbus
find /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.blob' | wc -l
/usr/local/bin/opblob inspect /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/zeroclaw.*.blob | sed -n '1,20p'
```

## Do Not Use Yet

- Do not use `deploy/s6/opdbus/run` yet. It has merge conflict markers.
- Do not normalize `Cargo.lock` casually. The workspace already had broad dirty lockfile state.

## Repo Status Notes

- `crates/op-blob/` is untracked in git.
- `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` are dirty.
- `Cargo.lock` has broad dependency churn from the current workspace state.

## Architecture Status

- SHM blobstore is now real and populated.
- Projection has not been converted yet.
- Next code step is projection reading `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs`, not `live-schema.json`.

- [Container Identity = sessionid](project_container_identity_is_sessionid.md) — a user container's id = container name = sessionid (one value, non-spoofable Argon2(PSK,salt=pubkey)); system containers use service name. createunixsocket --name and xray/bridge footprint all use it.
- [Call D-Bus, not URLs](feedback_call_dbus_not_urls.md) — operate via zbusctl/PluginService.CallMethod on the plugins path; don't grpcurl raw ip:port (bypasses identity, trips zero-trust).

- [Only Valid Path = Plugins](project_only_valid_path_plugins.md) — new backend capabilities register as plugins under org.dbus.v1.plugins (default_registry.rs → PluginService.CallMethod), NEVER as new operation.<domain>.v1.*Service proto packages. The 6 undefined frontend services (accountability/blockchain/agents-persona/stores/embedding) need plugins, not protos; btrfs already has one (wiring bug).
- [Gemma is a Plugin, not a Handler](project_gemma_plugin_not_handler.md) — Gemma → StatePlugin (gallery as projection, regenerate/delete as mutations via MutationEngine; inference stays op-gemma→Ollama). General rule: op-web handlers that read SHM bespoke or fork binaries belong as plugins/projections/mutations. Delete handlers/gemma.rs.
- [SHM Schema Layout](project_shm_schema_layout.md) — NAILED: folder of bare per-plugin schema objects + derived live-schema.json monolith + atomic manifest holding the one catalog_hash (leaf+fold, incremental); op-identity reads manifest hash, never re-hashes. Producer = op-projection SchemaEngine.write_schemas_to_shm.
- [One Schema / Single Source](project_one_schema_single_source.md) — FOUNDATIONAL: one schema, one source of truth, computed in exactly ONE place; a derivation (e.g. schema_catalog_hash) duplicated across files is the violation, not a constraint. Consolidate to one function.
- [No Container NIC or IP](project_no_container_nic_or_ip.md) — HARD RULE: no container gets a NIC/IP; all container I/O over UDS (socket passthrough / shared ovsbr0-sock); gRPC reflection works directly over UDS, never TCP host:port. 10.200.0.1/10.220.35.1 are HOST bridge addrs, not container endpoints.
- [Key Derivation](project_key_derivation.md) — RESOLVED: Argon2(secret=PSK, salt=WG pubkey); DB stores pubkey + UUID v5 token + blake3(psk) only; MAC provision-time only (invisible over WG); magic-link signup
- [Post Signals](feedback_post_signals.md) — proactively append suggestions/concerns/observations to SIGNALS.md (repo root); don't let model insight evaporate in chat
- [s6 Commit Prune Hazard](project_s6_commit_prune_hazard.md) — `s6 set commit` prunes the live-referenced compiled db (dangles bootdb, breaks /run/s6-rc state); ALWAYS commit+`live install` back-to-back; documented validated recovery
- [zeroclaw-gui Service](project_zeroclaw_gui_service.md) — native egui console at ~/.local/bin/zeroclaw-gui; s6 pipeline zeroclaw-gui-srv/-log on a private headless Xvfb :99 (no CRD/XFCE), software GL
- [Socket Provisioning](project_socket_provisioning.md) — use `zbusctl createsocket --name --port --path` (NOT raw `incus config device add proxy`) to expose container sockets; arch wants ONE shared socket (ovsbr0-sock) for all containers, OpenFlow/xray identity-routed
- [No Unfounded Generalizations](feedback_no_unfounded_generalizations.md) — never state blanket "X only does Y" claims as fact unless verified; scope tightly (e.g. "netmaker requires MQTT protocol, but broker impl is swappable"). User catches overgeneralizations.
- [SHM Reactive Principle](project_shm_reactive_principle.md) — system does NOT watch/poll/query/index/wait; /dev/shm is the authoritative present-state, components READ it; arrival (xray greeting connection) triggers action, not a watcher. Never design in poll-loops/watchers.
- [Wishlist Board](project_wishlist_board.md) — WISHLIST.md at repo root is the canonical assignable task board (Critical/Current/Next/Future/When-I-Have-Staff); prefer it over new TODO docs; Voyage→Qdrant export planned

- [Gemma 4 Perspectives](project_gemma_4perspectives.md) — Data/Numeric, Spatial/Layout, User Flow, Context/Aesthetic — 4 reasoning axes for schema-driven UI generation
- [3tched Architecture](project_3tched_architecture.md) — 31-crate Rust workspace; socket networking (Unix domain sockets + OVS OpenFlow); Incus containers; gRPC over UDS internally
- [WARP fwmark routing](feedback_warp_fmark.md) — WARP tunnel uses fwmark + table 51820, not default route; eth0 default route is separate
- [Artix Linux s6 layout](artix-s6-layout.md) — Artix s6-rc (NOT chimera); `s6` frontend CLI; service defs /etc/s6/sv/; env changes need recompile-and-update (live servicedir is frozen tmpfs copy); `s6 set commit -D default` avoids "bundle already defined"; op-web-srv readiness wedge holds global lock since boot
- [Compliance Architecture](project_compliance_architecture.md) — Btrfs+overlayfs+SHM CoW tiers; OSCAL-driven tag routing; three tag classes (OSCAL/3tched/UI); every mutation is enforcement point; enterprise/EU regulatory target
- [Cognitive MCP Architecture](project_cognitive_mcp_architecture.md) — cognitive-mcp is the universal gateway for ALL external clients (droid, NotebookLM, Cursor, Codex, Junie). Compact-mcp is loopback/chatbot only. Never suggest alternatives.
- [Identity Injection](project_identity_injection.md) — xraqy injects HTTP identity headers; WireGuard (grpc-uplink, 10.200.0.1) is transport only. Sub-HTTP protocols (NFS, raw TCP) must use the peer IP as identity anchor.
- [Zero Trust Principle](project_zero_trust_principle.md) — xraqy/WG identity header is the ONLY gate. IP ACLs, firewall rules, port restrictions are theater — mask them. Protocols that can't read the wristband header don't belong on the network surface.
- [Separate Commands](feedback_separate_commands.md) — Run bash commands as separate tool calls, not chained with && or ;
- [Incus Boot Wedge](project_incus_boot_wedge.md) — mail-3tched ERROR state blocks TTY boot; fix via live CD chroot + sqlite3 edit of local.db (do NOT use incus stop — causes global lock hang)
- [Storage Topology](project_storage_topology.md) — sda3=root(reinstalled), sdc=images(disk3.dd+image.dd), Incus pool=loop0; compliance_knowledge vectors lost in disk casualty; repomix sources intact on btrfs_out for re-ingest
- [Network Topology](project_network_topology.md) — netmaker=100.90.37.0/24, router=100.90.37.253(OpenWrt), laptop=172.16.0.124; grpc-uplink=10.200.0.x is separate from netmaker mesh
- [Compliance Agents](project_compliance_agents.md) — 8 new OSCAL/compliance agents in op-agents; memory/knowledge/schema_renderer/workflows added to always-loaded D-Bus plugins
- [MCP gRPC Transport](project_mcp_grpc_transport.md) — external MCP clients go through tonic-web gRPC (50052) + server reflection for tool discovery, not SSE/HTTP-3003; stdio→gRPC shim per CLI
- [xray Router](project_xray_router.md) — xray is the main router: OpenFlow tag routing + nginx/subdomain forwarding; oracle ingress is a decoy; config must be dynamic; next: add Gemma to stack
- [Voyage 4 Shared Embedding Space](reference_voyage4_shared_embedding_space.md) — production set = voyage-4 TRIO (large/4/lite), ONE 1024-dim shared space / one Qdrant collection / no re-index on switch. EXCLUDED: nano (512-dim), code-3 (deprecated — code re-vectorized into voyage-4), law-2 (separate domain space). Encoded in ctl_plane_chatbot VoyageModel.
- [Cognitive gRPC Endpoint](project_cognitive_grpc_endpoint.md) — live cognitive-mcp gRPC is 10.220.35.1:50052 (100.90.37.x stale); shim footprint/trace-id = client name, not WG pubkey; per-tool config file locations
- [Incus API Schema](reference_incus_api_schema.md) — official Incus instance/device schema from shared/api Go structs (NOT LXC); no first-class sockets field (proxy is a device type); 12 device types; socket↔container link by name; schematize via typed Device enum

Saved as a foundational memory. Here's what it changes concretely:

**The blob isn't a cache of the plugin — it's the plugin.** Existence = blob in the catalog. That means:

- **Registration and sealing are the same act.** `register_plugin_methods` sealing a blob isn't a "persist a copy" side effect to be deduplicated against `opblob seal-shm` — whichever one runs *is* the act of the plugin coming into being. The dual-writer question from the audit resolves itself: boot-time `seal-shm` materializes the plugin set, runtime registration mutates it, both are legitimate mutations of the one registry. What's illegitimate is any *reader* going around the catalog.
- **`DefaultPluginRegistry` is demoted to a behavior table.** Code answers "how do I execute method X" — never "does plugin X exist" or "what methods does it have." So `plugin_reader`'s current pattern (load plugins, call `.schema()`) is exactly backwards; projection enumerates the blob catalog and gets `BlobRef::plugin_schema()`, and only touches code at dispatch time.
- **`live-schema.json` isn't just legacy, it's a second self.** Every one of the 7 monolith consumers is asking a shadow copy of the plugin what the plugin is. Same for the identity hash: `catalog_hash` over the blob manifest *is* "which plugins exist," which is precisely what the WG/ghostbridge derivation wants to bind to.
- **Deregistration = removing the blob** — which is why the missing sweep in `seal_plugins` and the missing atomic manifest aren't polish items; without them the registry can assert plugins that don't exist.

The implementation order from the audit stands, just with a cleaner rule to check every step against: *no reader below the blob catalog*.

Only thing I need from you before touching code: the 12 conflicted files are your in-flight pr-17 merge, and several (op-dbus-mirror ×4, op-web ×3, ovs daemon) are unrelated to blobs. My read: resolve op-projection's two files blob-first (HEAD's manifest-writer as interim, drop pr-17's stale `blob.rs`), and resolve the rest by intent of each side. Confirm and I'll start.

import struct, json, hashlib

count = struct.unpack('<H', b[10:12])[0]
secs = {}
for i in range(count):
    e = 64 + i*24
    tag = struct.unpack('<I', b[e:e+4])[0]
    off, ln = struct.unpack('<QQ', b[e+8:e+24])
    secs[tag] = b[off:off+ln]
schema = json.loads(secs[1])

meta = json.loads(secs[4])
print("meta keys:", sorted(meta.keys()))
print("json_schema present:", 'json_schema' in meta and bool(meta['json_schema']))
EOF

import struct, json, glob
path = glob.glob('/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/wireguard.*.blob')[0]

b = open(path,'rb').read()
count = struct.unpack('<H', b[10:12])[0]
secs = {}
for i in range(count):
    e = 64 + i*24
    tag = struct.unpack('<I', b[e:e+4])[0]
    off, ln = struct.unpack('<QQ', b[e+8:e+24])
    secs[tag] = b[off:off+ln]
schema = json.loads(secs[1])
print("schema keys:", sorted(schema.keys()))
print("signals:", schema.get('signals'))
print("guarantees:", schema.get('guarantees'))
print("category:", schema.get('category'))
EOF

- All 14 pr-17 conflict resolutions (op-projection keeps the manifest writer + the identity schema-blob embed; op-dbus-mirror on the StateManager-excised side with the OVSDB feed rewired to `MutationEngine::change_tx` and the 300s heartbeat poll deleted; op-web on HEAD; deploy files on the pr-17 side since that's byte-for-byte what's live on the host).

content.text:
Verification is still running in the background, so this is my read on the design as it now stands — the shape of the thing is settled even while the last checks spin.

**I think you've landed on something coherent and unusually disciplined.** The final product is: one sealed artifact per plugin, one manifest as the commit point, and every consumer — reflection, routing, identity, web projection, the plugins reading their own desired state — answering "what exists and what can it do" from the same hash-verified bytes. After today there is no code path left that asks the Rust registry or a monolith file that question. That's the property that matters, and it now actually holds in the code rather than being an aspiration in a whitepaper.

What elevates it beyond a tidy refactor:

- **Existence and auth are the same fact.** The catalog hash feeding the WireGuard footprint means the plugin set is attested per-session. Very few systems can say "if you're authenticated, we agree about what software exists."
- **It deletes more concepts than it adds.** StateManager gone, heartbeat poller gone, dead re-hasher gone, NonNet publisher gone, the daemon deprecated in favor of a plugin. The system got *smaller* while gaining capability — the strongest signal an architecture is right rather than merely clever.
- **The failure modes are boring now.** A corrupt blob fails its hash and simply isn't advertised; a partial write is invisible behind rename(2); a vanished plugin is swept. No reconciliation loops, no cache invalidation, no "restart it and see."

What keeps it from being finished, honestly:

- The monolith **writers** still run. Until SchemaEngine's `live-schema.json` write and the duplicate `ShmWriter` are deleted, the old world can be resurrected by any future reader that greps for the file and finds it populated. The readers are migrated; the temptation isn't removed yet.
- **Nothing has been end-to-end verified live** — the migrated binaries haven't been rebuilt/redeployed, and the identity-hash switch needs that coordinated deploy moment. The design is sound; the deployment is the remaining risk.
- The **reduced working view** in op-blob and the qdrant_shuttle legacy reader are small residual dualities.

Net verdict: this is the rare refactor where the end state is simpler than the starting state and strictly more trustworthy. If the bot reviews come back quiet and the live deploy holds, I'd call the blob architecture done in substance — what remains is demolition, not construction. I'll commit and push the batch as soon as the checks report green.

content.text:
Pushed: `24550ea7..e38c48e3` — second batch is up for bot review.

On your point about btrfs snapshot + stream as the deployment unit — yes, that dissolves most of the concern I raised, and it's worth being precise about why:

**What it solves completely.** My worry was *version skew*: the sled writer, the ghostbridge verifier, and the sealer disagreeing about how `catalog_hash` is derived while a rolling deploy is half-finished. A btrfs send/receive stream makes the deployment unit atomic — binaries, service definitions, and the sealed blob image travel as one immutable snapshot, and the receiving host flips to it as a whole. There is no moment where the old op-identity-sled runs against a new bridge. Rollback is equally atomic: the previous snapshot is still there, and since your durability story is the mutation chain rather than state files, rolling back binaries doesn't strand any data — present state is just re-derived. It also composes with what op-blob already has: `btrfs-seal` puts the blob catalog *inside* a mountable image, so "which plugins exist" ships as part of the same artifact whose hash feeds identity. Deployment artifact = attested plugin set. That's tight.

**The one residue it doesn't remove:** the flip on the *running* host. Snapshots make the filesystem transition atomic, but processes holding the old world in memory don't atomically follow it — the running sled/bridge keep their old derivation until restarted, and `/dev/shm` (which is tmpfs, outside any btrfs snapshot) keeps the old catalog until the boot seal reruns. Practically that means the flip is: receive stream → restart the service set (or reboot). Since your s6 `op-dbus` run script already reseals SHM before exec, a coordinated `s6d restart` of the affected services after the stream lands is the whole remaining ceremony — one step, not a sequencing problem. The identity fallback chain I left in `schema_catalog_hash()` covers exactly that restart window and can be deleted once you're confident every host deploys this way.

So: agreed — with stream-based deployment, the "coordinated deploy" risk reduces to "restart services after receiving," which your tooling already handles. That, plus deleting the monolith writers next cycle, and I'd stop calling deployment a risk at all.
Removing the monolith writers now. First, a full sweep of what still touches `live-schema.json` or the legacy layout:

content.text:
Done and pushed: `8de1f19a..da4b3a8c`. Compile was green before the push this time.

Missing plugins now self-heal into SHM: at bridge startup, `seed_missing_plugin_projections` checks every loaded plugin against the sealed blob catalog and any plugin with a schema but no blob is blobified and sealed on the spot, with the catalog manifest committed through the same `BlobStore` path (so the hash and generation advance correctly). Existing blobs are never overwritten — the boot sealer's artifacts always win, and this only fills gaps.

That closes the full lifecycle, all four tasks complete:

- **Boot**: `opblob seal-shm` seals the full plugin set + manifest, sweeps stale blobs.
- **Startup gap-fill**: the bridge auto-seals anything the sealer missed (new plugin compiled in, catalog wiped, partial deploy).
- **Runtime**: `register_plugin_methods` seals on registration; reflection hydrates from the catalog on restart.
- **Reads**: every consumer — routing, reflection, identity hash, projections, plugins' own desired state — reads only sealed blobs and the manifest.

One honest caveat on the new auto-seal: it uses `BlobStore::open_default()` per startup, and if the boot sealer and bridge start concurrently both may write — writes are atomic per blob and per manifest so nothing tears, but the manifest generation may interleave. Same benign race noted earlier; a lock file is the eventual fix. Next real step remains deploying the rebuilt binaries (`s6d restart` after install, or the btrfs-stream path) so the live system runs what's now on `main`.
